correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed: the root has order n already modulo p, forcing Phi_n(q)=0 modulo p^k. A short sum produces an integer nonzero cyclotomic resultant by the Lam–Leung theorem, bounded above by (r-1)^phi(n) by all complex embeddings; the Sylvester identity forces divisibility by p^k. A geometric series gives exactly r terms. The logarithmic integer cutoff and n=2 boundary follow; 21 exact finite checks corroborate without replacing the proof.

value.rationale: The authors of the originating 2022 study specifically request a quantitative bound for their stabilization height K. This theorem gives a uniform explicit formula for all n and primes p=1 mod n and an effective global exceptional-prime cutoff, turning the existential finiteness into a concrete computationally usable theorem. It is a structural lifting barrier, not a standalone routine table or arbitrary numerical improvement. It does not claim optimality.
